## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of the per-particle update loop, combined with thread-level parallelism, can approach the streaming bandwidth ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
All measured N (10000–10000000) exceed the L2 spill at N≈7710, so the L1d (N≈481) and L2 transitions are below the sampled range. At q=0.01, ns/p is flat at 24.7–24.9 from N=10000 through N=100000 (both L3-resident), then rises modestly to 27.7–28.1 at N=1000000–10000000 as the working set crosses the L3→DRAM spill at N≈246723 — a ~12% knee, not a cliff. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: at q=0.5 the floor lifts to 32.7–36.8 ns/p, but the N-shape stays flat-with-DRAM-knee. No small-N amortization regime is visible since the smallest measured N is already past L2.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 2.75 GB/s at N=100000, q=0.01 — 21.7% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling. The algo is frontend-bound, not bandwidth-bound: perf attributes 67.9–76.5% of cycles to frontend stalls across all N and thread counts, with compute at 5–36% and backend stalls rising from 0.8% (L3) to 12–33% (DRAM) but never dominating. Bandwidth never approaches the ceiling at any regime; it falls further to 2.08 GB/s (16.4%) at q=0.5, but even at lowest churn the cap is instruction-fetch pressure, not memory.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within one particle, not across particles. The update loop (0x107f640) processes one particle per iteration with stride 0x44 (68 bytes), using `vmovups` (16-byte load/store), `vmovsd` (8-byte), `vmovss` (4-byte) to move the particle's floats, then `vmulps`/`vaddps` on the 4 components of that single particle. No gather — all loads are sequential from `[rdx+rcx+offset]`. The respawn/render loop uses byte-granular stores (`mov BYTE PTR [rsi+r14*1], sil`) — a scatter into a pixel buffer. The 491-instruction function with 34 `cmp`, 14 `je`, 12 `jne`, 11 `vucomiss` explains the persistent frontend stalls: branch-heavy control flow starves the fetch unit.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 2.75 GB/s (21.7% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling) even at q=0.01, because frontend stalls (67.9–76.5%) dominate across all regimes. Component-wise auto-vectorization within single particles (`vmulps` on 4 floats, stride 0x44) cannot approach the streaming ceiling; the 491-instruction branch-heavy step function caps throughput via instruction-fetch pressure rather than memory bandwidth.
